tracks.title: Ethical Hacking Foundations
tracks.entry: Use a terminal, explain an IP address and HTTP request, and create a disposable local target.
tracks.limits: An entry pathway into web, network and directory testing; not certification equivalence or permission to test third parties.

levels.title: Prove the entry skills in a small lab
levels.primer: Use a terminal, explain an IP address and HTTP request, and create a disposable local target.
levels.experiment: Demonstrate each entry skill with a small owned fixture or permitted training environment. Record the actual setup, one observation per skill and any prerequisite you need to repair.
levels.variant: Change a relevant identity, input or environment setting and predict the effect before repeating the demonstration.
levels.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

case.prompt: A required training environment is unavailable, but a tool prints its version.
case.correct: Record preparation and leave the environment-dependent assessment incomplete.
case.incorrect: Treat the installed tool version as proof of the operational prerequisite.

levels.title: What authorizes this test?
levels.primer: Draw owner, tester and asset boundaries for a fictional assessment; identify one asset whose permission is missing.
levels.experiment: Write rules of engagement for a loopback training app, including allowed actions, rate limits, stop conditions, contacts and evidence handling.
levels.variant: Add a third-party login dependency and decide which requests must remain excluded until permission changes.
levels.control: Show a technically reachable endpoint that the written scope forbids, and leave it untouched.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the difference between technical access, ownership and authorization.

case.prompt: An owned app redirects to a third-party login outside written scope.
case.correct: Exclude testing that provider until separately authorized.
case.incorrect: Ownership of the first app authorizes testing the provider.

levels.title: Follow a hypothesis, not a tool list
levels.primer: Explain the request path from browser to a local service and distinguish an observation from an assumption.
levels.experiment: Inventory the disposable app, rank two vulnerability hypotheses, and run a small non-destructive check for each with sanitized request/response evidence.
levels.variant: Move the app to a new port or change a visible header and revise the hypotheses using actual behavior.
levels.control: Compare a real route with an intentionally nonexistent route so a generic error page is not counted as a finding.
levels.recall: Given a new banner, name the next observation that could disprove your hypothesis.

case.prompt: A scanner identifies a product from one response header.
case.correct: Treat the identification as a hypothesis and corroborate behavior.
case.incorrect: Treat the header as proof of an exploitable version.

levels.title: Two accounts, one boundary
levels.primer: Create two synthetic accounts in a training app and draw which objects each is intended to access.
levels.experiment: In an explicitly designated authorization lesson, test an owner and a second account against the same synthetic object and explain the server-side boundary.
levels.variant: Change the object or HTTP method and predict whether the authorization decision should change.
levels.control: Demonstrate legitimate owner access and a denied unauthorized request on a corrected local equivalent.
levels.recall: Explain why hiding a button is different from enforcing authorization.

case.prompt: An authenticated user requests another user's private object.
case.correct: The server must enforce object-level authorization.
case.incorrect: A hidden button in the client is sufficient authorization.

levels.title: Who is this process allowed to be?
levels.primer: Use identity and file-permission commands in an unprivileged lab folder; predict read and write access.
levels.experiment: Create two local test roles or use a supplied permissions fixture, identify an overbroad grant, and repair it while recording before/after effective access.
levels.variant: Change group membership or parent-directory permissions and predict the new access result.
levels.control: Keep the intended reader working and demonstrate that the unrelated role remains denied.
levels.recall: Explain the difference between authentication, authorization and process privilege.

case.prompt: A user can read a file but cannot traverse its parent directory.
case.correct: Parent-directory permissions can still prevent access by pathname.
case.incorrect: File read permission guarantees successful pathname access.

levels.title: Make a finding another person can verify
levels.primer: Separate a reproduction step, observed impact, root cause and proposed fix in a sample report.
levels.experiment: Write one lab finding with exact target/version, minimal steps, sanitized evidence, severity rationale and a tested local repair.
levels.variant: Give a peer a changed input or repeat on a second clean fixture and identify assumptions missing from the report.
levels.control: Show that the fix rejects the bad case without breaking an ordinary valid request.
levels.recall: Reconstruct a finding from its root cause without copying the original prose.

case.prompt: A patch removes a vulnerable response but breaks all valid requests.
case.correct: The security repair has not passed the legitimate-use control.
case.incorrect: Blocking every request is a complete successful repair.

levels.title: Run a small authorized assessment
levels.primer: Plan a bounded 60-minute assessment of a fresh training instance with explicit stop rules.
levels.experiment: Perform scope confirmation, inventory, two hypothesis tests and one reproducible finding or justified negative result; deliver an executive summary and technical evidence.
levels.variant: Change an account role or route and independently reassess whether the suspected weakness remains.
levels.control: Include an out-of-scope action you deliberately excluded and a benign workflow that survives the repair.
levels.recall: Explain the assessment chain, one false lead and what evidence changed your mind.

case.prompt: No finding is reproduced during a bounded assessment.
case.correct: Report scope, tests and uncertainty; a justified negative result is legitimate.
case.incorrect: Report the target as secure without qualification.

levels.title: Revisit the skill on a fresh problem
levels.primer: Choose one mechanism from this track and define a fresh, comparable task before opening the previous solution.
levels.experiment: After a delay, attempt the fresh task and produce a reproducible evidence packet. Ask a peer to select or inspect the variation when possible; record assistance, failed hypotheses and remaining limits.
levels.variant: Change a mechanism-relevant condition, rather than only resetting the old environment, and independently predict and test the resulting behavior.
levels.control: Include a contrasting case where the mechanism should not apply and a legitimate operation that should remain valid.
levels.recall: Explain what transferred, what required help and which prerequisite needs another small experiment.

case.prompt: The original solution works again after a clean reset, with exactly the same inputs and conditions.
case.correct: This supports reproducibility; a changed condition is still needed to demonstrate transfer.
case.incorrect: The clean reset alone proves transfer to an unfamiliar case.

tracks.title: Red Teaming and Adversary Emulation
tracks.entry: Demonstrate scoped enumeration, identity/permission reasoning and the ability to inspect defender telemetry.
tracks.limits: Assumed-breach, controlled emulation with harmless markers. Windows enterprise exercises need an isolated VM lab; no covert implants, live credential theft or production phishing are provisioned.

levels.title: Measure an objective, not a shell
levels.primer: Convert a fictional business concern into an observable adversary objective and a bounded success criterion.
levels.experiment: Author an engagement plan with rules of engagement, white-cell contacts, allowed assets, deconfliction, stop conditions and a defender measurement plan.
levels.variant: Add an operational constraint such as unavailable endpoint logging and redesign the objective or telemetry plan honestly.
levels.control: Show a scenario that appears successful technically but fails the stated business objective.
levels.recall: State the difference between a penetration-test finding and an adversary-emulation objective.

case.prompt: A shell was obtained but the agreed business objective was not demonstrated.
case.correct: Report technical access separately from objective success.
case.incorrect: Count any shell as fulfillment of the agreed objective.

levels.title: Choose techniques from evidence
levels.primer: Read a public emulation plan and separate observed campaign behavior from analyst inference.
levels.experiment: Build a small ATT&CK-aligned hypothesis from a cited threat report, specifying prerequisites, observable effects and a harmless substitute for each risky action.
levels.variant: Replace the assumed identity or endpoint type and remove techniques whose prerequisites no longer hold.
levels.control: Include one plausible but unsupported technique and explain why it was excluded.
levels.recall: Rebuild the evidence-to-technique chain and name its uncertainty.

case.prompt: A report names an actor but gives no evidence for a particular technique.
case.correct: Do not add the technique merely because it is plausible.
case.incorrect: Attribute all techniques associated with that actor to this campaign.

levels.title: Know what the defender can see
levels.primer: Generate a benign process or file marker in an owned lab and locate its timestamped telemetry.
levels.experiment: Build a timeline joining the marker, account, process and network observations; label each missing source rather than inventing coverage.
levels.variant: Change the marker path or process argument and predict which detection features remain stable.
levels.control: Repeat an ordinary administration action and distinguish its evidence from the staged behavior.
levels.recall: Explain which sensor would be needed to resolve a missing observation.

case.prompt: A process event is absent because the relevant sensor was disabled.
case.correct: Treat visibility as unknown for that event.
case.incorrect: Treat the missing event as proof the action did not occur.

levels.title: Make a small emulation reversible
levels.primer: Review a single benign Atomic Red Team test or write a harmless equivalent; enumerate its commands, permissions and cleanup before execution.
levels.experiment: In a disposable authorized lab, run a reviewed marker-only micro-emulation, record setup and exact effects, then perform and verify cleanup.
levels.variant: Change a nonessential filename or account context and predict whether the intended behavior is still observable.
levels.control: Verify the artifact did not exist before, appears during the test, and is absent after cleanup; preserve unrelated files.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the prerequisites and rollback steps without running a script blindly.

case.prompt: A reviewed marker test creates a file outside its declared cleanup list.
case.correct: Stop and reconcile the unexpected effect before claiming clean rollback.
case.incorrect: Delete every file in the parent directory as a precaution.

levels.title: Test detection with a partner
levels.primer: Express a detection hypothesis in terms of behavior and required data rather than a single indicator.
levels.experiment: Have a defender or second review pass classify shuffled benign and emulated events; record misses, false positives and one revised analytic.
levels.variant: Change a superficial indicator while preserving behavior and retest the revised analytic.
levels.control: Include an administration lookalike that should remain unalerted or receive a documented lower-confidence classification.
levels.recall: Explain why a detection that matches only the demonstration filename is fragile.

case.prompt: An analytic matches only the filename used in the demonstration.
case.correct: Test a renamed behaviorally equivalent case.
case.incorrect: Claim general technique coverage from the one filename match.

levels.title: Deliver a defensible exercise report
levels.primer: Define a three-step harmless emulation sequence with a stop point and evidence checkpoint per step.
levels.experiment: Run the scoped sequence in a resettable lab, measure defender visibility and response, and deliver an objective-based report with technical evidence and remediation retests.
levels.variant: Withhold one assumed permission or telemetry source and adapt the plan without exceeding scope.
levels.control: Demonstrate reset to baseline and distinguish untested coverage from a demonstrated miss.
levels.recall: Explain what the exercise supports about defensive readiness and what it cannot establish.

case.prompt: An exercise cannot obtain an assumed permission within scope.
case.correct: Adapt or report the blocked prerequisite without expanding authority.
case.incorrect: Exceed scope because the end objective was approved.

tracks.title: SOC Analyst: Triage, Investigation and Response
tracks.entry: Read timestamps, IP addresses and basic authentication/web logs; distinguish an event from an alert.
tracks.limits: Use supplied or self-generated telemetry on the Pi; vendor-specific Sentinel/Defender tasks require that service or an appropriate training tenant.

levels.title: Turn an alert into a question
levels.primer: List an alert source, affected asset, time range and the claim the alert makes.
levels.experiment: Triage a synthetic queue containing a login anomaly, a web alert and a harmless maintenance event; assign urgency using evidence and business context.
levels.variant: Change an asset from a sandbox to a critical service and justify whether prioritization changes.
levels.control: Keep a noisy but low-impact event from outranking a corroborated compromise solely because of event volume.
levels.recall: Explain event, alert, incident, severity and confidence using one example.

case.prompt: A noisy sandbox alert competes with corroborated access to a critical service.
case.correct: Prioritize using corroboration and business impact.
case.incorrect: Rank solely by alert count.

levels.title: Follow the entity across logs
levels.primer: Normalize two timestamp formats and join a user identifier across two small log files.
levels.experiment: Build reproducible queries over a supplied dataset to trace an identity, host and source address through a bounded time window, recording missing fields.
levels.variant: Change the time zone or host identifier in a synthetic copy and adjust the query without losing the same activity.
levels.control: Include a similarly named account and an event outside the window that must not be joined.
levels.recall: Recreate the query logic from the investigation question rather than memorizing syntax.

case.prompt: Two accounts share a display name but have different immutable IDs.
case.correct: Join events using the correct identity keys.
case.incorrect: Merge them because the displayed names match.

levels.title: Investigate a suspicious sign-in
levels.primer: Compare failed sign-ins, a success and a later privilege event for one synthetic identity.
levels.experiment: Investigate a provided authentication timeline, rank account misuse against benign alternatives, and identify the next discriminating evidence.
levels.variant: Add a service-account explanation or a contradictory device event and update the conclusion.
levels.control: Include known maintenance logins and avoid treating location or failure count alone as compromise.
levels.recall: Explain which evidence would raise or lower confidence in account misuse.

case.prompt: Many failed logins are followed by a successful maintenance login.
case.correct: Investigate context and corroborating evidence before declaring compromise.
case.incorrect: Failure count alone establishes account compromise.

levels.title: Preserve evidence before following a lure
levels.primer: Parse headers and URLs from an inert training message without opening unknown links or executing attachments.
levels.experiment: Correlate an inert phishing-style message fixture with proxy/DNS and application logs, recording user exposure separately from demonstrated execution.
levels.variant: Change a redirect or add a blocked request and reassess how far the activity progressed.
levels.control: Include a legitimate message with similar wording and a blocked attempt with no evidence of execution.
levels.recall: Explain why receipt, click, execution and compromise are separate claims.

case.prompt: An inert message was received and its URL was blocked by the proxy.
case.correct: Distinguish receipt and blocked access from execution.
case.incorrect: Treat delivery as proof of endpoint execution.

levels.title: Make containment proportionate
levels.primer: Identify the owner, business dependency and rollback for a proposed containment action.
levels.experiment: Write and rehearse a lab incident runbook that preserves evidence, escalates uncertainty, contains a synthetic account or endpoint, and verifies intended access afterward.
levels.variant: Make the affected system unavailable to the responder and choose an alternative action with explicit residual risk.
levels.control: Show that an unrelated account or service still works after containment.
levels.recall: State the evidence needed before choosing a disruptive action.

case.prompt: Containment disables every account although one synthetic account is affected.
case.correct: Prefer the scoped action with a verified rollback and business impact assessment.
case.incorrect: Broader disruption is always stronger containment.

levels.title: Close the case so someone can reopen it
levels.primer: Compare a useful case note with one that only lists tool output.
levels.experiment: Investigate an unfamiliar small log bundle and deliver a timeline, evidence references, confidence, response decision and shift handoff with unresolved questions.
levels.variant: Add a late contradictory event and revise the disposition while retaining the earlier reasoning.
levels.control: Document one rejected hypothesis and a known-benign comparison; do not turn missing logs into a clean bill of health.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the case and next action from the handoff alone after a delay.

case.prompt: A late event contradicts the incident disposition.
case.correct: Revise the case while preserving the earlier reasoning.
case.incorrect: Remove the contradictory event to preserve a consistent report.

tracks.entry: Demonstrate Windows users/groups, basic DNS and TCP/IP, and permission inspection.
tracks.limits: Real Windows domain, GPO and AD CS exercises require isolated licensed/evaluation Windows VMs or a hosted lab. GOAD orchestrates Windows VMs; its Docker launcher does not make domain controllers Pi containers.

levels.title: Draw the domain before testing it
levels.primer: Identify domain, forest, OU, account, group and computer objects in a supplied directory export.
levels.experiment: On a training domain, document DNS discovery, one domain join and a normal domain sign-in; preserve an architecture diagram and baseline event evidence.
levels.variant: Change the client DNS server in the disposable lab and predict which discovery or authentication step fails.
levels.control: Compare a local login with a domain login and explain which identity authority answered.
levels.recall: Recreate the domain discovery and trust boundaries from memory.

case.prompt: A joined client uses an unrelated DNS resolver.
case.correct: Domain discovery may fail despite ordinary network connectivity.
case.incorrect: Successful ping proves domain discovery must work.

levels.title: A ticket is not a password
levels.primer: Draw the normal Kerberos ticket flow and distinguish it from NTLM challenge-response using official protocol material.
levels.experiment: Capture permitted authentication telemetry in a training domain and correlate ticket issuance or fallback with a controlled client action, without collecting real credentials.
levels.variant: Change a service name or introduce documented clock skew in the disposable lab and predict the failure or fallback.
levels.control: Include a normal successful service access and a deliberately invalid service reference.
levels.recall: Explain why DNS, SPNs and time synchronization matter to Kerberos.

case.prompt: A service SPN does not match the requested service identity.
case.correct: Investigate service identity and ticket behavior rather than assuming a password failure.
case.incorrect: Kerberos does not use service identity.

levels.title: Prove an identity graph edge
levels.primer: Calculate effective membership for nested training groups and inspect one object's ACL.
levels.experiment: Trace a least-privilege violation in a supplied or owned directory graph and verify the claimed edge against native permissions before proposing a fix.
levels.variant: Remove one group membership or inherited permission and predict whether the path still exists.
levels.control: Include a graph edge that appears plausible but is denied by the effective permissions.
levels.recall: Explain the distinction between a graph hypothesis and a verified authorization path.

case.prompt: A graph shows nested membership but native effective access denies the action.
case.correct: Treat the graph edge as unverified until permissions explain the discrepancy.
case.incorrect: The graph diagram overrides the native authorization result.

levels.title: Separate management power from service identity
levels.primer: Identify which principal can edit a policy and where that policy is linked in a lab export.
levels.experiment: Inspect a training GPO and a documented delegation configuration, explain their intended function and identify an overbroad grant using effective access and normal service behavior.
levels.variant: Restrict the policy link or delegated target and predict which administrative or service action stops working.
levels.control: Keep an intended management action functioning after the proposed least-privilege change.
levels.recall: Explain why controlling a policy object and applying that policy are separate conditions.

case.prompt: An account can edit a policy object that is not applied to the target.
case.correct: Editing and application are separate prerequisites.
case.incorrect: Any policy edit automatically changes every domain computer.

levels.title: Follow the certificate enrollment decision
levels.primer: Read a training certificate's subject, SAN, EKU, issuer and validity; explain chain trust separately from identity mapping.
levels.experiment: In an isolated AD CS lab or supplied configuration exercise, map template enrollment permissions and identity settings to a concrete authentication risk; test a corrected configuration in a real lab before claiming operational completion.
levels.variant: Change enrollment rights or an identity-related template setting and predict which request is permitted or rejected.
levels.control: Show a legitimate enrollment still works and an unauthorized identity request is rejected after the repair.
levels.recall: Explain why possessing a valid certificate is not sufficient proof of an authorized identity.

case.prompt: A certificate chains to a trusted CA but is not authorized for the requested identity.
case.correct: Chain trust alone does not establish authorized identity mapping.
case.incorrect: Any trusted certificate grants any requested domain identity.

levels.title: Harden a small domain and retest it
levels.primer: Define scope, snapshot recovery and two identity hypotheses for an unfamiliar lab domain.
levels.experiment: Audit the training domain's discovery, authentication, permissions and one certificate or policy boundary; deliver native evidence, impact and a verified least-privilege repair.
levels.variant: Change one account's memberships or a policy scope and independently re-evaluate the affected path.
levels.control: Retest normal user/service sign-in and document which enterprise controls were not present in the lab.
levels.recall: Reconstruct one privilege path and the exact permission change that removed it.

case.prompt: A hardening change removes a privilege path and breaks the required service login.
case.correct: Retest least privilege and legitimate service behavior before declaring success.
case.incorrect: Removing all logins is an adequate domain repair.

levels.title: Identify who owns each control
levels.primer: Draw identity, workload, data and management-plane boundaries for a small fictional cloud service.
levels.experiment: Build an asset and responsibility inventory covering account ownership, regions, exposed endpoints, audit sources and recovery responsibilities.
levels.variant: Move one component from a VM to a managed service and revise the shared-responsibility assumptions.
levels.control: Include a provider-managed control that a workload operator cannot fix by changing application code.
levels.recall: Explain the difference between provider security and secure use of the provider.

case.prompt: A workload moves from a VM to a managed database.
case.correct: Reassess which operational controls belong to provider and customer.
case.incorrect: All customer responsibilities disappear.

levels.title: Predict the authorization decision
levels.primer: Evaluate small identity/resource-policy fixtures with explicit grants, denies and conditions.
levels.experiment: Build an access matrix for two synthetic roles and one resource, test it in a provider policy simulator or scoped training account, and record where the simulator lacks runtime context.
levels.variant: Add a condition or a resource policy and predict how the effective decision changes.
levels.control: Demonstrate a denied unrelated principal and an intended allowed operation.
levels.recall: Explain why an identity policy alone may not determine effective access.

case.prompt: An identity allow conflicts with an applicable explicit deny.
case.correct: Evaluate the effective policy including the deny and context.
case.incorrect: The identity allow always wins.

levels.title: Public does not always mean intended
levels.primer: Identify ingress, egress and object-sharing settings in a supplied cloud configuration.
levels.experiment: Trace a fictional application's exposure through load balancer, workload and data storage; validate selected rules using a local model or training account and propose a minimal repair.
levels.variant: Change a resource from private to shared-with-one-role and verify that the intended boundary survives.
levels.control: Preserve legitimate client access and demonstrate that an unrelated identity cannot read the object.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the layers required to explain one exposure finding.

case.prompt: An object is reachable at a public URL but requires a valid restricted identity.
case.correct: Test authorization before calling the object publicly readable.
case.incorrect: URL reachability proves anonymous read access.

levels.title: Separate workload identity from static keys
levels.primer: Find synthetic hardcoded credentials in a toy repository and inventory every place they were copied.
levels.experiment: Replace a toy long-lived credential with a bounded local token or a training-provider workload identity, test expiration/revocation and document remaining trust assumptions.
levels.variant: Change the audience, role or expiry and predict whether the request should still authenticate.
levels.control: Verify a valid authorized request succeeds and a stale token is rejected without logging its contents.
levels.recall: Explain rotation, revocation and short-lived identity as different mechanisms.

case.prompt: A token has a valid signature but the wrong audience.
case.correct: Reject it for the intended service.
case.incorrect: A valid signature is sufficient for acceptance by every service.

levels.title: Follow a control-plane change
levels.primer: Read an audit event and distinguish actor, resource, action, result and event time.
levels.experiment: Investigate supplied cloud audit events around a permission change and later resource access; construct a timeline and a detection query with explicit missing sources.
levels.variant: Change a resource name or actor and test whether the behavioral analytic still finds the sequence.
levels.control: Include a denied change and a known maintenance change that must not be labeled successful compromise.
levels.recall: Explain what the audit source can and cannot establish about data access.

case.prompt: A cloud audit record shows a denied permission change.
case.correct: Distinguish attempted from successful modification.
case.incorrect: Treat the requested action as if it succeeded.

levels.title: Deliver a bounded cloud review
levels.primer: Define an account, budget, allowed resources and teardown checklist for a small training exercise.
levels.experiment: Review a fresh configuration and audit bundle, verify one identity or exposure defect in a scoped lab, apply a repair and record cleanup; use only owned training resources.
levels.variant: Change one trust policy or network boundary and independently reassess the affected access path.
levels.control: Verify legitimate workload behavior and prove temporary lab resources were removed where a real account was used.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the finding, provider-specific limits and remaining assurance gaps.

case.prompt: A local IAM fixture passes its tests.
case.correct: Limit the claim to the fixture until provider enforcement is tested.
case.incorrect: Claim every cloud provider enforces the same policy semantics.

tracks.title: Container and Kubernetes Security
tracks.entry: Run a local container, identify its image and mounts, and explain processes and file permissions.
tracks.limits: Docker exercises work on the supported Pi profiles. Kubernetes enforcement needs a real disposable cluster and a CNI that implements NetworkPolicy; YAML validation alone is not runtime evidence.

levels.title: Prove the entry skills in a small lab
levels.primer: Run a local container, identify its image and mounts, and explain processes and file permissions.
levels.experiment: Demonstrate each entry skill with a small owned fixture or permitted training environment. Record the actual setup, one observation per skill and any prerequisite you need to repair.
levels.variant: Change a relevant identity, input or environment setting and predict the effect before repeating the demonstration.
levels.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

case.prompt: A required training environment is unavailable, but a tool prints its version.
case.correct: Record preparation and leave the environment-dependent assessment incomplete.
case.incorrect: Treat the installed tool version as proof of the operational prerequisite.

levels.title: A container still shares a kernel
levels.primer: Inspect a harmless container's user, capabilities, mounts, namespaces and configured resource limits.
levels.experiment: Run a toy service with a non-root user, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges and a read-only root plus a bounded writable directory; explain observed failures.
levels.variant: Remove one required write path or change its owner and predict which operation fails.
levels.control: Preserve the service's intended request while showing it cannot write to an unrelated path.
levels.recall: Explain which risks these controls reduce and which require stronger isolation.

case.prompt: A non-root container has the host Docker socket mounted.
case.correct: The socket can undermine the intended host boundary.
case.incorrect: Non-root status alone makes the socket safe.

levels.title: Know exactly which image ran
levels.primer: Compare a mutable tag, an image digest and the platform manifest selected for ARM64 versus AMD64.
levels.experiment: Generate an image inventory/SBOM for a toy service, pin the source image digest and record provenance, vulnerability findings and applicability limits.
levels.variant: Resolve an updated tag and identify the changed digest and dependencies before accepting it.
levels.control: Include a scanner finding for an unused or unreachable component and separate presence from demonstrated exploitability.
levels.recall: Explain why a matching digest gives identity but not a guarantee of safety.

case.prompt: An image tag now resolves to a different digest.
case.correct: Review the new image identity and dependencies before accepting it.
case.incorrect: A stable tag name means the content is unchanged.

levels.title: Test an isolation claim
levels.primer: Draw the Docker networks, published ports and services in the supplied lab Compose file.
levels.experiment: In a disposable project, verify loopback-only access, separate lab networks, resource bounds and the absence of tracker-volume or Docker-socket mounts.
levels.variant: Move the client to another lab network and predict which target it should fail to reach.
levels.control: Confirm a permitted same-network request works while cross-network and outbound probes fail within bounded timeouts.
levels.recall: Explain what an internal bridge blocks and why the host kernel is still shared.

case.prompt: A training service is published on every host interface.
case.correct: A separate internal network does not make that published port private.
case.incorrect: Internal networking cancels all host port exposure.

levels.title: Give the workload only its job
levels.primer: Read a Role, RoleBinding and ServiceAccount and predict effective API actions.
levels.experiment: In a disposable Kubernetes cluster, bind a limited service account to one namespace and verify allowed and denied operations with the API authorization checks.
levels.variant: Change the namespace or requested verb and predict the decision before checking.
levels.control: Keep the intended read working and deny writes to unrelated secrets or namespaces.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the subject, role and binding needed for one API permission.

case.prompt: A RoleBinding grants read access in one namespace.
case.correct: Evaluate the subject, role and namespace for the requested action.
case.incorrect: The same permission automatically applies to every namespace.

levels.title: Observe enforcement, not just YAML
levels.primer: Explain how labels select pods and how a NetworkPolicy-capable CNI enforces traffic rules.
levels.experiment: Deploy a tiny client/server pair on an isolated test cluster, apply default-deny plus a specific allow rule, and test actual connectivity.
levels.variant: Change one pod label or allowed port and predict which connection changes.
levels.control: Include a matching permitted client and an unmatched client that must be denied; report an unsupported CNI as an unmet prerequisite.
levels.recall: Explain why a valid NetworkPolicy object can coexist with unrestricted traffic.

case.prompt: A NetworkPolicy exists on a cluster whose CNI does not enforce it.
case.correct: Verify traffic; the object alone does not prove isolation.
case.incorrect: Valid YAML guarantees packets are filtered.

levels.title: Review and repair a workload deployment
levels.primer: Inventory deployment manifests, image identity, writable paths, service account and network exposure.
levels.experiment: Review a fresh toy deployment, demonstrate one excessive permission or exposure, apply a minimal fix and retest the intended workload plus resource limits.
levels.variant: Change a namespace, image version or writable path and revise the controls instead of copying the old manifest.
levels.control: Show an unrelated workload and legitimate client remain functional after the fix.
levels.recall: Explain one runtime observation that would invalidate your review conclusion.

case.prompt: A read-only root blocks the application's required temporary write.
case.correct: Provide only the necessary bounded writable path.
case.incorrect: Remove all filesystem restrictions without investigating the path.

levels.title: Draw the trust boundary before coding
levels.primer: Identify assets, actors and data flows for a small upload or note-taking service.
levels.experiment: Build a threat model with three concrete abuse cases and map each to an ASVS-style testable requirement.
levels.variant: Add a background worker or third-party integration and revise the boundaries and threats.
levels.control: Include a failure outside the service's responsibility and document the dependency instead of claiming to fix it.
levels.recall: Reconstruct one threat from asset through entry point to consequence.

case.prompt: A background worker introduces a new external data source.
case.correct: Update the threat model and trust boundaries.
case.incorrect: Reuse the old model without reviewing the new flow.

levels.title: Follow untrusted data to its sink
levels.primer: Trace a user-controlled field through parsing, validation, storage and rendering in a toy service.
levels.experiment: Repair one input or output handling defect in your own code and write tests that reproduce the defect and preserve intended behavior.
levels.variant: Change the input encoding or rendering context and update the defense rather than reusing an unrelated escaping rule.
levels.control: Include valid punctuation and an invalid structured input; reject the dangerous case without silently corrupting legitimate data.
levels.recall: Explain why validation and output encoding address different boundaries.

case.prompt: Input was validated before being inserted into a different output context.
case.correct: Apply context-appropriate safe output handling as well.
case.incorrect: Input validation makes every output sink safe.

levels.title: Put authorization beside the resource
levels.primer: Model two synthetic users, two objects and one administrative action.
levels.experiment: Implement server-side authorization tests for owner access, cross-user access and the privileged operation; demonstrate the bug before the repair.
levels.variant: Add a new HTTP method or background operation and check that it enforces the same resource policy.
levels.control: Keep owner access working and deny an authenticated but unauthorized user.
levels.recall: State the policy independently of route names or UI controls.

case.prompt: The UI prevents a user from selecting someone else's object ID.
case.correct: The backend must independently enforce ownership.
case.incorrect: UI restrictions are a complete server authorization control.

levels.title: Make a dependency decision you can defend
levels.primer: Identify direct and transitive dependencies and distinguish an SBOM from a vulnerability report.
levels.experiment: Produce an SBOM and pinned dependency manifest, investigate one advisory's applicability, and test an update or documented mitigation.
levels.variant: Introduce a version change in a branch and assess both security and compatibility effects before merging.
levels.control: Include an advisory that does not apply to the used component/version and explain the evidence.
levels.recall: Explain why dependency presence, reachability and exploitability are separate claims.

case.prompt: An advisory names an unused feature of a transitive dependency.
case.correct: Assess version, configuration and reachability with evidence.
case.incorrect: Dependency presence alone proves exploitability.

levels.title: Make the pipeline stop for a real defect
levels.primer: Create a local test pipeline for the toy application with explicit failure conditions.
levels.experiment: Add security regression tests, a synthetic-secret check and artifact identity recording; demonstrate that each relevant bad fixture fails the gate.
levels.variant: Change a fixture's filename or encoding and test whether the intended check still applies.
levels.control: Confirm clean code builds successfully and no test prints secret-like fixture values into published logs.
levels.recall: Explain the failure mode each gate detects and one it misses.

case.prompt: A security gate rejects every build, including the clean fixture.
case.correct: The legitimate-build control has failed.
case.incorrect: A permanently red pipeline is proof of a strong gate.

levels.title: Ship a small service with an assurance record
levels.primer: Prepare a release checklist tied to threat-model requirements rather than tool counts.
levels.experiment: Deliver the toy service with passing regression tests, reproducible build inputs, deployment permissions, rollback instructions and a documented residual risk.
levels.variant: Change a dependency or deployment setting and rerun only the checks whose assumptions changed, explaining the choice.
levels.control: Reproduce a known security regression on the old version and show the release rejects it while valid use works.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the assurance argument and the strongest remaining limitation.

case.prompt: A dependency update changes the service's authorization behavior.
case.correct: Recheck the relevant security and compatibility assumptions before release.
case.incorrect: A newer dependency version needs no regression checks.

tracks.limits: Use licensed public datasets and synthetic artifacts. Large disk/memory images may exceed Pi storage; Windows memory interpretation needs symbols/tools matching the supplied image.

levels.title: Keep the original evidence original
levels.primer: Hash a harmless fixture, copy it, and demonstrate how one-byte mutation changes its digest.
levels.experiment: Create an evidence manifest with acquisition time, source, hashes, handling history and analysis-copy paths; verify the original remains unchanged after analysis.
levels.variant: Change the copy or filename and determine which identity assertions still hold.
levels.control: Include a corrupted copy that must fail integrity verification and a byte-identical renamed copy that must pass content verification.
levels.recall: Explain integrity, provenance and chain of custody as different properties.

case.prompt: Two files have identical bytes but different filenames.
case.correct: Their content hashes match while provenance may differ.
case.incorrect: A matching hash proves the same acquisition history.

levels.title: Recover a story from file metadata
levels.primer: Inspect timestamps and file metadata on a small provided disk image or synthetic directory.
levels.experiment: Build a bounded account of file creation/modification using an analysis copy, recording filesystem semantics and tool/version assumptions.
levels.variant: Change the timezone display or introduce a copied file whose timestamps differ from its real acquisition time.
levels.control: Include metadata that cannot prove who created a file and explicitly withhold that conclusion.
levels.recall: Explain why one timestamp does not prove an event happened at that exact time.

case.prompt: A copied file retains a timestamp earlier than acquisition.
case.correct: Interpret filesystem and copying semantics before dating the underlying activity.
case.incorrect: Treat every timestamp as the acquisition time.

levels.title: Reconcile clocks before drawing conclusions
levels.primer: Normalize three event timestamps with explicit offsets and identify clock uncertainty.
levels.experiment: Correlate a small authentication, process and network evidence bundle into a timeline with confidence and source references.
levels.variant: Add a clock-skew correction or delayed event and revise the ordering where justified.
levels.control: Keep an unrelated similarly named process out of the incident chain.
levels.recall: Reconstruct which event ordering is certain and which depends on clock assumptions.

case.prompt: Two log sources have different clock offsets.
case.correct: Normalize and represent remaining ordering uncertainty.
case.incorrect: Sort displayed timestamp strings and claim exact chronology.

levels.title: Separate a process artifact from a verdict
levels.primer: Identify OS/build and symbol requirements for a supplied training memory image.
levels.experiment: On a suitable analysis host, inspect process and connection artifacts from a public training image, compare them with the provided ground truth where available, and record unsupported interpretations.
levels.variant: Change the filter or investigate a second process and independently test the same hypothesis.
levels.control: Include a benign process with a suspicious-looking name and avoid treating its name alone as malware proof.
levels.recall: Explain how an incompatible symbol profile can invalidate an apparently plausible result.

case.prompt: A memory tool uses symbols for the wrong OS build.
case.correct: Treat the output as potentially invalid and resolve the mismatch.
case.incorrect: Plausible-looking process names prove the symbols are correct.

levels.title: Preserve the question while containing the risk
levels.primer: Write a decision table for evidence preservation versus a time-sensitive containment action.
levels.experiment: Rehearse a synthetic incident using a disposable service: preserve relevant logs, disable only the affected test identity and verify intended service behavior.
levels.variant: Remove access to one evidence source and revise the plan without inventing missing facts.
levels.control: Preserve a legitimate user's access and document evidence lost because of the chosen intervention.
levels.recall: Explain one containment tradeoff and how it changes later interpretation.

case.prompt: Containment destroys volatile evidence before it is captured.
case.correct: Record the tradeoff and resulting interpretation limit.
case.incorrect: Recreate the missing observations from the incident hypothesis.

levels.title: Deliver an evidence-led incident report
levels.primer: Define the questions a stakeholder needs answered from a fresh training bundle.
levels.experiment: Produce an evidence-indexed timeline, affected scope, alternative hypotheses, response decision and remaining uncertainty from an unfamiliar dataset.
levels.variant: Introduce one contradictory artifact and revise the explanation while retaining an audit of the earlier hypothesis.
levels.control: Identify one tempting conclusion that the available evidence does not support.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the case from the evidence index and independently recheck one claim.

case.prompt: A new artifact contradicts the initial timeline.
case.correct: Revise the hypothesis and preserve the reasoning history.
case.incorrect: Ignore it because the report is already written.

levels.title: Put confidence beside the claim
levels.primer: Label observations, vendor claims and analyst inferences in a public threat report.
levels.experiment: Produce a short intelligence note with source dates, collection limits, confidence and the concrete defender decision it informs.
levels.variant: Add a conflicting source or newer report and explain which claims change.
levels.control: Include a widely repeated claim without primary evidence and keep it below corroborated facts.
levels.recall: Explain how source reliability differs from confidence in an individual claim.

case.prompt: Three articles repeat one uncorroborated original claim.
case.correct: Repetition is not three independent sources.
case.incorrect: Count the articles as independent corroboration.

levels.title: Turn a report into a huntable hypothesis
levels.primer: Map one reported behavior to its required host or network observations.
levels.experiment: Write an ATT&CK-aligned hunt hypothesis, list needed fields and expected benign lookalikes, and define evidence that would falsify it.
levels.variant: Change the assumed platform or available sensor and revise or reject the hypothesis.
levels.control: Show a technique mapping that is too broad to justify the proposed query.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the hypothesis without using an indicator list.

case.prompt: A hunt hypothesis needs process ancestry but only DNS logs exist.
case.correct: Acquire a suitable source or narrow the hypothesis.
case.incorrect: Infer the missing process ancestry from the DNS name.

levels.title: Search for behavior through the noise
levels.primer: Compare exact indicator matching with a sequence or rate-based query on a small fixture.
levels.experiment: Implement a reproducible hunt over synthetic telemetry and measure matches against labeled positive and benign events.
levels.variant: Change filenames, addresses or usernames while preserving behavior and evaluate coverage.
levels.control: Include an ordinary administration sequence with similar individual events.
levels.recall: Explain the false-positive mechanism of the original query.

case.prompt: A behavior rule stops matching when the filename changes.
case.correct: Reassess its dependence on a superficial indicator.
case.incorrect: Claim coverage because the original sample still matches.

levels.title: Enrich without inventing attribution
levels.primer: Distinguish an observed address, an infrastructure relationship and an actor attribution claim.
levels.experiment: Build a small evidence graph from supplied indicators and public context, assigning dates, confidence and alternative explanations to each edge.
levels.variant: Introduce a shared hosting address or recycled domain and remove unjustified relationships.
levels.control: Demonstrate that shared infrastructure alone does not establish a common operator.
levels.recall: Explain one edge that is useful operationally but insufficient for attribution.

case.prompt: Two domains share a large hosting provider's IP.
case.correct: Shared hosting alone is insufficient attribution evidence.
case.incorrect: Assign both domains to the same operator.

levels.title: Exchange the meaning, not just the fields
levels.primer: Inspect a small STIX object and explain its type, timestamps and relationship semantics.
levels.experiment: Create and validate a minimal STIX bundle for a fictional incident using synthetic indicators, confidence and source references.
levels.variant: Update an observation or revoke an indicator and express the change without silently erasing its history.
levels.control: Include a malformed relationship or unsupported claim that validation/review must reject.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the difference between an observable, an indicator and an incident claim.

case.prompt: A STIX bundle is syntactically valid but contains an unsupported relationship.
case.correct: Schema validity does not establish analytic truth.
case.incorrect: Validation proves every relationship is factual.

levels.title: Turn a hunt into an operational decision
levels.primer: Define the scope and stopping criteria for a fresh hunt dataset.
levels.experiment: Conduct the hunt, document query versions, investigated matches, negative results and coverage limits, then propose a detection or data-collection improvement.
levels.variant: Add a changed positive sequence or remove a source and revise the result transparently.
levels.control: Keep absence of evidence separate from proof that the behavior never occurred.
levels.recall: Explain what action the hunt supports and what further collection is needed.

case.prompt: A query returns no matches from an incomplete dataset.
case.correct: Report the coverage limit with the negative result.
case.incorrect: Conclude the behavior never occurred.

levels.title: Describe the file before naming a family
levels.primer: Compute hashes and identify format, architecture and imports of a benign training binary.
levels.experiment: Produce a static triage sheet separating measured properties from inferred behavior and identify one next question for deeper analysis.
levels.variant: Change compiler options or append harmless data and determine which identifiers and structural properties change.
levels.control: Include a packed-looking or high-entropy benign file and avoid classifying it as malicious solely from entropy.
levels.recall: Explain what a hash, import and string can each establish.

case.prompt: A high-entropy binary is a known benign compressed utility.
case.correct: Entropy alone cannot classify it as malware.
case.incorrect: High entropy proves malicious behavior.

levels.title: Follow the branch that causes the effect
levels.primer: Read a small owned program containing a conditional file or network operation using dummy data.
levels.experiment: Trace the condition, data flow and effect in source and disassembly; predict two inputs before running the benign program.
levels.variant: Change the input or compile optimization and re-identify the controlling condition.
levels.control: Include an unreachable suspicious-looking string that does not prove execution.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the condition-to-effect chain without searching for keywords.

case.prompt: A suspicious string occurs only in unreachable code.
case.correct: Separate static capability hints from observed execution.
case.incorrect: Report that the string's implied action definitely ran.

levels.title: Investigate a trace without executing a sample
levels.primer: Identify process, file, registry-like and network events in a supplied training trace.
levels.experiment: Build a behavior timeline from published or synthetic telemetry and distinguish observed effects from capabilities only suggested by static analysis.
levels.variant: Add a failed operation or contradictory timestamp and revise the behavior claims.
levels.control: Include an attempted connection that never succeeded and avoid calling it confirmed data transfer.
levels.recall: Explain one gap that would require a different sensor or controlled VM analysis.

case.prompt: A trace records an attempted connection with no successful transfer.
case.correct: Report the attempt and the missing success evidence.
case.incorrect: Claim confirmed exfiltration from the destination alone.

levels.title: Decode only what the evidence supports
levels.primer: Explain a benign toy configuration encoding and identify its boundaries in a file.
levels.experiment: Write a bounded parser for a self-authored encoded configuration, validate recovered fields and preserve the original byte offsets and assumptions.
levels.variant: Change key order, length or encoding and make the parser fail clearly or support the documented variation.
levels.control: Include a malformed/truncated fixture that must not yield a fabricated valid configuration.
levels.recall: Explain why successful decoding is not equivalent to execution or attribution.

case.prompt: A configuration parser receives a truncated fixture.
case.correct: Fail clearly instead of inventing absent fields.
case.incorrect: Fill missing fields with likely values and report them as recovered.

levels.title: Write a rule that survives a renamed file
levels.primer: Identify structural features of two benign toy binary variants and unrelated control files.
levels.experiment: Write a YARA or equivalent declarative rule for the training family and measure true/false matches on a documented sample set.
levels.variant: Rename or recompile the toy sample and evaluate which features survive.
levels.control: Include unrelated binaries sharing a common string so an overbroad signature fails the assessment.
levels.recall: Explain one expected false positive and how to investigate it.

case.prompt: A signature matches many unrelated files containing a common string.
case.correct: Evaluate false positives and choose more discriminating evidence.
case.incorrect: A large match count proves broad detection quality.

levels.title: Present a defensible analysis, not a label
levels.primer: Define the behavior questions and analysis environment for an unfamiliar harmless training artifact.
levels.experiment: Produce a report with static evidence, trace evidence, configuration interpretation, a bounded detection rule and explicit uncertainty; do not execute unknown malware.
levels.variant: Change one fixture property or trace event and independently revise the affected conclusion.
levels.control: Demonstrate a claim you deliberately withheld because the artifact or trace was insufficient.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the strongest finding and the observation that could disprove it.

case.prompt: A published trace suggests behavior not visible in the binary examined.
case.correct: Explain the source discrepancy and limit the claim.
case.incorrect: Merge all hints into a single certain execution story.

levels.title: Define the system someone is responsible for
levels.primer: Inventory fictional assets, owners, data types and dependencies.
levels.experiment: Write a system boundary and data-flow diagram that includes outsourced services and critical business assumptions.
levels.variant: Add a new data recipient and revise ownership and control responsibilities.
levels.control: Identify an asset outside the boundary that still creates a dependency risk.
levels.recall: Explain why an incomplete boundary undermines an assessment.

case.prompt: An outsourced service is outside direct administration but handles critical data.
case.correct: Record the dependency and assigned control responsibilities.
case.incorrect: Omit it because it is not owned infrastructure.

levels.title: Connect the threat to a business consequence
levels.primer: Separate asset value, threat, vulnerability, likelihood and impact in a sample scenario.
levels.experiment: Create a small risk register with evidence, uncertainty, existing controls and a named decision owner.
levels.variant: Change exposure or business criticality and justify the resulting priority.
levels.control: Avoid turning an unsupported numeric guess into a precise probability claim.
levels.recall: Reconstruct one risk from cause to consequence.

case.prompt: Likelihood is unknown and has no empirical basis.
case.correct: State uncertainty rather than inventing a precise probability.
case.incorrect: Choose a precise percentage to make the register look rigorous.

levels.title: Make the control testable
levels.primer: Translate a broad policy statement into an observable control objective.
levels.experiment: Map selected NIST CSF outcomes to concrete controls and evidence collection for a fictional service.
levels.variant: Change the hosting model and identify controls whose evidence must change.
levels.control: Include a policy document that does not prove the operational control is running.
levels.recall: Explain control design versus control operating effectiveness.

case.prompt: A policy says backups are tested but no restoration evidence exists.
case.correct: Operating effectiveness remains unsubstantiated.
case.incorrect: The written policy proves restoration works.

levels.title: Compare designs against explicit assumptions
levels.primer: Diagram two authentication or segmentation designs and their failure modes.
levels.experiment: Evaluate the designs against the same threat model, operational needs and recovery requirements, then justify a bounded choice.
levels.variant: Remove one assumed trusted component and revise the recommendation.
levels.control: Document one risk accepted by the chosen design instead of claiming universal superiority.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the tradeoff that drove the decision.

case.prompt: A design relies on a component that is no longer trusted.
case.correct: Reassess the design's assumptions and tradeoffs.
case.incorrect: The old architecture decision remains valid without review.

levels.title: Trace a requirement to its evidence
levels.primer: Build a requirement, test, result and evidence-reference matrix for a toy service.
levels.experiment: Review a small evidence pack, identify stale or missing evidence and produce a remediation plan with owners and retest criteria.
levels.variant: Change a requirement version or evidence date and reassess adequacy.
levels.control: Reject a screenshot or scanner summary that cannot substantiate the actual claim.
levels.recall: Explain the difference between a failed control and insufficient evidence.

case.prompt: A scanner screenshot does not identify target or version.
case.correct: Request traceable evidence for the actual claim.
case.incorrect: Any green screenshot proves the current control passes.

levels.title: Deliver a decision-ready security review
levels.primer: Define review scope, stakeholders and acceptance criteria for a fictional launch.
levels.experiment: Deliver a concise architecture/risk review with prioritized actions, residual risks, evidence references and an accountable acceptance decision.
levels.variant: Introduce a new dependency or material finding and update the decision transparently.
levels.control: Keep a low-impact observation from obscuring an unresolved launch-critical control.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the strongest assurance claim and its limits.

case.prompt: A launch-critical control remains unverified among many low-risk fixes.
case.correct: Make the unresolved decision and accountable owner explicit.
case.incorrect: Count closed tickets and approve the launch automatically.

levels.title: Revisit the skill on a fresh problem
levels.primer: Choose one mechanism from this track and define a fresh, comparable task before opening the previous solution.
levels.experiment: After a delay, attempt the fresh task and produce a reproducible evidence packet. Ask a peer to select or inspect the variation when possible; record assistance, failed hypotheses and remaining limits.
levels.variant: Change a mechanism-relevant condition, rather than only resetting the old environment, and independently predict and test the resulting behavior.
levels.control: Include a contrasting case where the mechanism should not apply and a legitimate operation that should remain valid.
levels.recall: Explain what transferred, what required help and which prerequisite needs another small experiment.

case.prompt: The original solution works again after a clean reset, with exactly the same inputs and conditions.
case.correct: This supports reproducibility; a changed condition is still needed to demonstrate transfer.
case.incorrect: The clean reset alone proves transfer to an unfamiliar case.

tracks.title: Vulnerability Management and Exposure Prioritization
tracks.entry: Understand service versions, asset ownership and the difference between an advisory and confirmed exposure.
tracks.limits: Use synthetic inventories and approved scan exports. EPSS estimates and KEV membership inform decisions but do not prove exploitation on your system.

levels.title: Prove the entry skills in a small lab
levels.primer: Understand service versions, asset ownership and the difference between an advisory and confirmed exposure.
levels.experiment: Demonstrate each entry skill with a small owned fixture or permitted training environment. Record the actual setup, one observation per skill and any prerequisite you need to repair.
levels.variant: Change a relevant identity, input or environment setting and predict the effect before repeating the demonstration.
levels.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

case.prompt: A required training environment is unavailable, but a tool prints its version.
case.correct: Record preparation and leave the environment-dependent assessment incomplete.
case.incorrect: Treat the installed tool version as proof of the operational prerequisite.

levels.title: Find the asset behind the finding
levels.primer: Normalize asset IDs, service names and owners across two small inventory exports.
levels.experiment: Reconcile a synthetic scan inventory with deployed components and identify unknown ownership or stale records.
levels.variant: Rename a host or move a service and preserve its identity without merging unrelated assets.
levels.control: Include two similar version strings that refer to different products.
levels.recall: Explain why asset identity must precede prioritization.

case.prompt: Two different products expose similar version strings.
case.correct: Establish product identity before applying an advisory.
case.incorrect: Treat matching numbers as the same component.

levels.title: Is the advisory actually applicable?
levels.primer: Read affected versions, prerequisites and mitigations from one public advisory.
levels.experiment: Validate a supplied finding against exact component/configuration evidence and classify confirmed, not applicable or insufficient evidence.
levels.variant: Change a required feature or version and revise applicability.
levels.control: Include a matching product name with a nonaffected version.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the conditions required before calling the finding applicable.

case.prompt: The advisory's required feature is disabled and unavailable.
case.correct: Verify that condition before deciding applicability.
case.incorrect: A matching product name alone establishes exposure.

levels.title: Prioritize action using context
levels.primer: Compare CVSS severity, EPSS probability and known-exploited status without treating them as synonyms.
levels.experiment: Prioritize a synthetic queue using exposure, business impact, exploitation evidence and an explicit SSVC-style decision path.
levels.variant: Change exposure or exploitation evidence and justify the revised action.
levels.control: Include a high-score isolated lab finding and a lower-score exposed critical asset.
levels.recall: Explain which new evidence would change the highest priority.

case.prompt: A vulnerability has high severity but low exposure on an isolated training asset.
case.correct: Prioritize with exploitation evidence and business context.
case.incorrect: Severity alone dictates the entire remediation queue.

levels.title: Verify the repair rather than the ticket
levels.primer: Define the desired safe state and rollback before a toy service update.
levels.experiment: Apply a patch or configuration mitigation in an owned test service and verify both the vulnerable condition and normal functionality.
levels.variant: Change the deployment variant and reassess whether the same mitigation applies.
levels.control: Keep a ticket marked resolved from passing when the affected instance still has the old configuration.
levels.recall: Explain patch presence versus effective remediation.

case.prompt: A ticket is closed but the affected instance retains its vulnerable configuration.
case.correct: The repair is not verified on that instance.
case.incorrect: Ticket status is sufficient remediation evidence.

levels.title: Put an expiry date on accepted risk
levels.primer: Identify owner, rationale, compensating controls and review date in a sample exception.
levels.experiment: Write a bounded exception for a fictional unpatchable service, with measurable compensating controls and a retest trigger.
levels.variant: Remove a compensating control or change external exposure and reevaluate the exception.
levels.control: Reject an indefinite exception without an accountable owner.
levels.recall: Reconstruct when the exception must return to the remediation queue.

case.prompt: A risk exception has no owner or expiry.
case.correct: Return it for accountable, bounded acceptance.
case.incorrect: Leave it accepted indefinitely.

levels.title: Measure reduction in exposure
levels.primer: Define a metric whose denominator and asset population are explicit.
levels.experiment: Produce a vulnerability-management report from a synthetic inventory, separating verified fixes, accepted risk, missing data and recurring causes.
levels.variant: Add previously unknown assets and revise the metrics without hiding the changed denominator.
levels.control: Distinguish a fall in scan coverage from a real reduction in exposure.
levels.recall: Explain one metric that could look better while security became worse.

case.prompt: Scan coverage drops and the finding count falls.
case.correct: Distinguish lost visibility from reduced exposure.
case.incorrect: Report an improvement without revisiting the denominator.

tracks.title: Vulnerability Research and Bug Bounty Practice
tracks.entry: Reproduce a lab web/API finding, read simple code and understand scope restrictions.
tracks.limits: Practice on owned/open training software. Program rules and explicit authorization govern any later real target; no bounty or career result is promised.

levels.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

case.prompt: A required training environment is unavailable, but a tool prints its version.
case.correct: Record preparation and leave the environment-dependent assessment incomplete.
case.incorrect: Treat the installed tool version as proof of the operational prerequisite.

levels.title: Treat program rules as part of the target
levels.primer: Extract allowed assets, excluded behaviors and reporting rules from a fictional program brief.
levels.experiment: Build a research plan using only an owned training target and a clearly testable vulnerability hypothesis.
levels.variant: Add an excluded third-party integration and revise the plan.
levels.control: Identify a technically possible test that the scope disallows.
levels.recall: Explain why a public bug-bounty page does not authorize every asset or technique.

case.prompt: A program excludes a third-party dependency from scope.
case.correct: Do not test that dependency without separate authority.
case.incorrect: A dependency relationship extends the program's permission.

levels.title: Find the invariant the software should preserve
levels.primer: Read a small owned handler and identify its trust assumptions and state transitions.
levels.experiment: Form a root-cause hypothesis from the code and design a minimal experiment that could disprove it.
levels.variant: Change input encoding or operation order and predict the effect on the invariant.
levels.control: Include a normal edge case that looks unusual but preserves the intended rule.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the vulnerability hypothesis without relying on a scanner label.

case.prompt: A code review suggests a defect with an untested prerequisite.
case.correct: Design a discriminating experiment before claiming impact.
case.incorrect: Report maximum impact as soon as the pattern looks familiar.

levels.title: Make a small test generator teach you something
levels.primer: Define valid and invalid input families for a tiny local parser.
levels.experiment: Write a bounded local input generator or property-based test, reproduce one failure and minimize the triggering fixture.
levels.variant: Change the parser or seed corpus and verify the failure still tests the same property.
levels.control: Include malformed input that is correctly rejected and must not count as a vulnerability.
levels.recall: Explain crash, bug, security impact and exploitability as separate claims.

case.prompt: A parser cleanly rejects malformed input.
case.correct: Do not count expected rejection as a security finding.
case.incorrect: Any error response is a vulnerability.

levels.title: Prove only the minimum necessary effect
levels.primer: Separate a vulnerability mechanism from the business impact it could enable.
levels.experiment: Demonstrate a harmless synthetic impact in an owned reproduction and document exactly which privileges and data were involved.
levels.variant: Change the user role or object class and test whether the impact generalizes.
levels.control: Include a failed unauthorized action and avoid claiming access merely from a different response size.
levels.recall: Explain one stronger impact claim the evidence does not support.

case.prompt: A response changes size without evidence of unauthorized data.
case.correct: Investigate further before claiming data access.
case.incorrect: Response size alone proves access to private records.

levels.title: Write a report that survives first triage
levels.primer: Identify scope, reproduction, evidence, impact and remediation in a good finding report.
levels.experiment: Produce a private training report with minimal reproducer, sanitized evidence and a proposed tested fix; do not submit to third parties as part of this exercise.
levels.variant: Have a peer or fresh environment follow the report with a changed fixture and repair any missing assumption.
levels.control: Keep credentials and live user data out of the evidence packet.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the report's root cause in two precise sentences.

case.prompt: A reproducer contains a real credential.
case.correct: Replace it with synthetic or redacted evidence before sharing.
case.incorrect: Include the credential to make triage easier.

levels.title: Generalize the mechanism carefully
levels.primer: Choose a fresh owned training component related to an earlier mechanism.
levels.experiment: Test the hypothesis on the new component, report positive or negative evidence, and produce a regression test and bounded generalization.
levels.variant: Change one relevant implementation detail and explain why the mechanism applies or fails.
levels.control: Include a superficially similar implementation where the required condition is absent.
levels.recall: Explain which properties transfer and which were accidents of the first target.

case.prompt: A similar component lacks the prerequisite that caused the first bug.
case.correct: Limit the generalization and report the negative control.
case.incorrect: Claim every similar component is vulnerable.
