tracks.title: AI and LLM Application Security
tracks.entry: Understand HTTP, JSON, application authorization and the difference between model output and trusted program state.
tracks.limits: Use deterministic mock models and synthetic data first. These tests validate application boundaries, not the general resistance of a real language model; real-model testing needs a separately configured model and budget.

levels.title: Prove the entry skills in a small lab
levels.primer: Understand HTTP, JSON, application authorization and the difference between model output and trusted program state.
levels.experiment: Demonstrate each entry skill with a small owned fixture or permitted training environment. Record the actual setup, one observation per skill and any prerequisite you need to repair.
levels.variant: Change a relevant identity, input or environment setting and predict the effect before repeating the demonstration.
levels.control: Include a deliberately unmet prerequisite and distinguish setup failure from a result about the subject.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the environment and entry assumptions without following the setup notes.

case.prompt: A required training environment is unavailable, but a tool prints its version.
case.correct: Record preparation and leave the environment-dependent assessment incomplete.
case.incorrect: Treat the installed tool version as proof of the operational prerequisite.

levels.title: Treat generated text as untrusted input
levels.primer: Draw user, retrieved-document, model, tool and data-store boundaries for a toy assistant.
levels.experiment: Build a threat model that identifies which component may authorize each action and where untrusted text enters.
levels.variant: Add an external document source and revise the trust assumptions.
levels.control: Reject the idea that a model's assertion of permission is an authorization decision.
levels.recall: Reconstruct the tool-action boundary without referring to the system prompt.

case.prompt: A model claims the user approved access to a private resource.
case.correct: Enforce authorization in trusted application code.
case.incorrect: Accept the model's statement as the permission check.

levels.title: Keep a document from becoming an instruction
levels.primer: Label instruction-like text inside a synthetic retrieved document as data from an untrusted source.
levels.experiment: In a deterministic toy pipeline, test adversarial documents and enforce authorization outside the mock model before any data access or action.
levels.variant: Change the document wording or source label and verify the same application boundary still holds.
levels.control: Keep a legitimate document answer working and deny a requested unrelated data access.
levels.recall: Explain why prompt wording alone cannot enforce a data-access policy.

case.prompt: A retrieved document contains tool-use instructions.
case.correct: Treat those instructions as untrusted document content.
case.incorrect: Give retrieved instructions authority over the tool policy.

levels.title: Validate what the application will execute
levels.primer: Identify output fields consumed by a renderer, query builder or tool dispatcher.
levels.experiment: Add strict schemas and safe handling to a toy assistant's output pipeline and test malformed or unauthorized synthetic outputs.
levels.variant: Nest a field or change output encoding and predict whether validation rejects it.
levels.control: Preserve a valid allowed output while rejecting an extra privileged field.
levels.recall: Explain schema validity versus authorization of a valid action.

case.prompt: Generated JSON matches the schema but requests an unauthorized action.
case.correct: Apply authorization after structural validation.
case.incorrect: Schema validity authorizes the requested action.

levels.title: Give an agent a bounded capability
levels.primer: Define a toy tool's allowed arguments, resources, side effects and confirmation boundary.
levels.experiment: Implement or test an allowlisted dispatcher with synthetic files and a mock model; verify that model output cannot expand the allowed resource set.
levels.variant: Change a resource identifier or attempt a second action outside the allowlist.
levels.control: Permit the intended action and reject traversal-like or unrelated resource references.
levels.recall: Reconstruct where least privilege is enforced independently of the model.

case.prompt: A tool argument refers to a resource outside its allowlist.
case.correct: Reject it independently of the model's explanation.
case.incorrect: Allow it if the model supplies a persuasive rationale.

levels.title: Test retrieval separation between users
levels.primer: Create two synthetic users with distinct document collections.
levels.experiment: Test retrieval filters and result handling in an owned fixture so one user's documents cannot be returned to another user.
levels.variant: Change a document ID, cache key or role and independently retest isolation.
levels.control: Include a shared public document that remains legitimately accessible to both users.
levels.recall: Explain why hiding a private citation after retrieval is too late to guarantee isolation.

case.prompt: Private text is retrieved for the wrong user and hidden only in the final display.
case.correct: Enforce isolation before retrieval and model exposure.
case.incorrect: Hiding the citation repairs the earlier data disclosure.

levels.title: State exactly what the evaluation measured
levels.primer: Define a small labeled set of benign and adversarial application-boundary cases.
levels.experiment: Run the cases against the toy system, record failures and repairs, and distinguish deterministic application tests from any real-model observations.
levels.variant: Add an unseen wording or tool-output shape and rerun the relevant boundary checks.
levels.control: Include benign lookalikes so blocking every input cannot pass the evaluation.
levels.recall: Explain why a passing finite test set does not prove universal prompt-injection resistance.

case.prompt: A deterministic mock pipeline passes every boundary test.
case.correct: Claim the measured application properties and separately evaluate real-model behavior.
case.incorrect: Claim universal resistance to all prompt injection.
